messages:
alex: FYI: after the queue_shaping heuristic flip last night we see a ~3.2% p95 latency regression on continuous-batcher for text-generation workloads. RMS baseline was stable; this correlates with a rise in tiny-microbatch frequency. Canary shows same.

sam: I profiled the hot path. Kernel choice is flipping more often on small joins; we end up on the slower GEMM path for ~40% of microbatches. Short dump from the perf collector: 

```json
{"batch_size_dist": {"1": 0.41, "2": 0.28, "4": 0.18, "8":0.13}, "kernel_selected": "gelu_gemm_slow"}
```

jin: Also seeing KV prefix cache hit-rate drop on the same hosts. prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.69 -> 0.31 after the heuristic change. KV churn went up ~3x; eviction_rate spiked. My hypothesis: more tiny batches are producing many short-lived prefixes, causing cache-line fragmentation and lower locality.

perf-bot: ALERT: p95 latency increased 3.1% (baseline 120ms -> 123.7ms) on pool gpu-rtf-4; cpu_wait increased 12%; continuous_batcher.small_batch_fraction increased from 0.18 -> 0.43.

marcus: Can we rule out network scheduling? queue_depth metrics look stable across racks. If kernel selection + cache thrash is the culprit, a rollback of queue_shaping on canary seems prudent.

alex: Agreed. I'll roll the flag to false on canary (config: continuous_batcher.queue_shaping=false). Will monitor prefix_cache.hit_rate and kernel_choice histograms and postback.

sam: If rollback fixes it we should follow up with two changes: bump token_budget_target by +20% to reduce tiny-batch formation, and widen pack-by-latency window by +10ms to give the packer more time.

jin: Also propose a short-term KV mitigation: pin frequently-accessed prefixes for 30s when detection sees repeated tiny batches for an origin; reduces eviction churn.

alex: Rolling now. tagging @oncall for watch. :eyes:
